reference:
But the book made Heidi even more unhappy as it told a story of a dying
old woman. She thought of Grannie and feared she might have died.
Heidi couldn't stop sobbing or hide her feelings. "I'm afraid I won't be able
to see Grannie. I miss my grandfather. I want to go back to the mountain."
The house was haunted by rumors about a ghost.
"I know this will scare Clara but I have no choice," she told herself while
planning her next move. So she told Clara and Heidi about the ghost. She
hoped this would make Clara ask her father for help. And it did.
and waited, and finally the "ghost"
appeared.
It was Heidi.
"So, you are homesick," he said. "But don't you cry to ease the sadness?"
The doctor suggested Heidi have a good cry. "That girl needs to go home to
be cured," he then told Mr. Seemann.
After careful thought, Mr. Sesemann decided it was right to send Heidi back
to her grandfather's. He then told Clara his decision.
